intro: winch is a server configuration tool. It describes the desired state of your servers in declarative YAML and provides commands to manage that state.

blocks.text: A project is a directory with a winch.yaml file and the inventories, pipelines, and recipes that it uses. winch reads the project in the current directory.
Minimal project
One winch.yaml with a name, a host, and one step:

# winch.yaml
name: demo
hosts:
  web1.example.com:
    address: 192.0.2.10
steps:
  - name: Write the message of the day
    file:
      path: /etc/motd
      content: "Managed by winch.\n"
Check it, show the changes, then make them:

winch validate
winch plan
winch apply

# winch writes /etc/motd on web1.example.com.
Hosts

winch connects with the OpenSSH client and its SSH config. The login user is root, or has passwordless sudo. A host needs nothing else installed: winch sends a helper program to /var/lib/winch/ on the host and runs it there. Run winch doc remote.
When the project grows
Move the hosts into inventories, the steps into pipelines, and groups of steps into recipes:

winch.yaml               the project file
inventories/
  production.yaml        an inventory: hosts and groups
  test.yaml
pipelines/
  site.yaml              a pipeline: stages and steps
recipes/
  nginx/
    recipe.yaml          a recipe: variables, steps, and handlers
    templates/site.tmpl  the templates of the recipe
    files/tls.conf       the files of the recipe
The name of an inventory or a pipeline is its file name without .yaml. Plan and apply then name the pipeline: winch plan site.
An inventory, a pipeline, or a recipe can also be a key in winch.yaml, under inventories, pipelines, or recipes. The value of the key is the content of the file. A name in both places is an error.
Top-level inventory and pipeline

hosts and groups at the top of winch.yaml are the only inventory of the project. They work with any number of pipelines. steps, handlers, parallelism, and health at the top of winch.yaml are the only pipeline. Then plan and apply take no pipeline name.
YAML

All files are YAML 1.2. Only true and false are booleans: yes, no, on, and off are strings. File modes are strings: mode: "0644". Unknown keys and duplicate keys are errors. Anchors and aliases work. Merge keys (<<) do not. winch fmt fixes the indentation and the step key order.

keys.name: name
keys.text: Letters, digits, ., _, and -. It does not start with a dot. Hosts keep pending handlers and other state of the project under this name.

keys.name: inventory
keys.text: Default for --inventory. A project with more than one inventory and no default makes every run name its inventory with --inventory.

keys.name: recipients
keys.text: Age public keys. winch encrypts each secret for all of them. winch secret init adds a key.

keys.name: ssh_config
keys.text: Path of an SSH config file, relative to the project directory. winch passes it to every ssh with -F, and ssh reads it instead of ~/.ssh/config. The file can have the line Include ~/.ssh/config. Run winch doc remote.

keys.name: vars
keys.text: Shared variable defaults, by name. A default can be a !secret, an !expr, or a !tpl. Run winch doc variables.

keys.name: inventories
keys.text: Inventories kept in winch.yaml, by name. The value of each is the content of an inventory file, as in inventories/<name>.yaml.

keys.name: pipelines
keys.text: Pipelines kept in winch.yaml, by name. The value of each is the content of a pipeline file, as in pipelines/<name>.yaml.

keys.name: recipes
keys.text: Recipes kept in winch.yaml, by name. The value of each is the content of a recipe file, as in recipes/<name>/recipe.yaml. Such a recipe has no templates/ or files/ directory. Its steps cannot use template, source, or the key of repo.

keys.name: hosts
keys.text: Hosts of the only inventory, as in an inventory file. The project then has no other inventory. It can have any number of pipelines.

keys.name: groups
keys.text: Groups of the only inventory, as in an inventory file.

keys.name: steps
keys.text: Steps of the only pipeline. It has one stage on all hosts, and both have the name of the project. The project then has no other pipeline. Plan and apply take no pipeline name.

keys.name: handlers
keys.text: Handlers of the only pipeline, as in a pipeline file.

keys.name: parallelism
keys.text: Parallelism of the only pipeline, as in a pipeline file.

keys.name: health
keys.line: health gate of the only pipeline
keys.text: Health gate of the only pipeline, as in a pipeline file.

blocks.text: An inventory lists the hosts that winch manages, puts them in groups, and gives them values.
Files
An inventory is a file in inventories/, such as inventories/production.yaml, or a key in inventories of winch.yaml. It holds data and secrets, but no templates or expressions.
Choosing the inventory

--inventory <name> names the inventory of a run. inventory in winch.yaml names a default. A project with one inventory uses it. A project with more inventories and no default makes each run name its inventory, so a run against production is always deliberate.
Groups and values

The group all contains every host. A host value beats a group value, and a group value beats a value of all. Two groups of one host that set different values for one variable, or for user, are an error, unless the host sets that value too.
SSH settings
Every other SSH setting, such as the port or the key, comes from your SSH config. Its Host blocks match the host name, also when the host has an address.
Host patterns
Host patterns select hosts in the hosts of a stage, in --hosts, and in winch run and winch exec:

rows: the hosts in the group web, or the host named web
the hosts in web or in db
the hosts in web and in prod
the hosts in web, without web3

blocks.text: & and ! bind tighter than ",". Hosts keep inventory order. A name that is neither a group nor a host is an error. A pattern with only ! names is an error: write all & !web, not !web.

# inventories/production.yaml
hosts:
  mail.acme.com:
    address: 192.0.2.10
  monitor.acme.com:
    address: 192.0.2.20
groups:
  all:
    user: admin
    vars:
      domain: acme.com
  mail:
    hosts: [mail.acme.com]
    vars:
      mail_server: true

# winch.yaml
name: acme
vars:
  domain: example.com
  mail_server: false
steps:
  - name: Install postfix on the mail servers
    pkg:
      name: postfix
    when: !expr vars.mail_server

keys.name: hosts
keys.text: Keyed by host name. Without address, the name is the SSH host name. A host name that YAML reads as a number, such as 1234, needs quotes. A host and a group cannot have the same name.

keys.name: address
keys.line: host name or IP for SSH
keys.text: Host name or IP for SSH. Without it, the SSH config decides the host name, and host.address is the name of the host. The Host blocks of the SSH config match the host name, also with address. A port goes in the SSH config. Two hosts cannot have the same SSH host name, port, and jump host.

keys.name: user
keys.text: SSH login user. Without it, the host takes the user of its groups, then of all, then of the SSH config. --user beats it. Every other SSH setting comes from your SSH config.

keys.name: vars
keys.text: Variable values of the host. They beat the values of its groups.

keys.name: groups
keys.text: Keyed by group name. The group all contains every host. A host value beats a group value, and a group value beats a value of all.

keys.name: user
keys.line: SSH login user of the members
keys.text: SSH login user of the members. Two groups of one host with different users are an error, unless the host sets user.

keys.name: hosts
keys.text: Member host names. The group all cannot have hosts. A group can be empty: hosts: [].

keys.name: vars
keys.text: Variable values of the members. Two groups of one host that set different values for one variable are an error, unless the host sets that value too.

topics.name: pipeline
topics.line: ordered stages that apply steps to hosts

blocks.text: A pipeline is an ordered list of stages. Each stage applies its steps to a set of hosts.
Files
A pipeline is a file in pipelines/, such as pipelines/site.yaml, or a key in pipelines of winch.yaml. winch plan site and winch apply site run it.
One stage or many

Most pipelines run the same steps on every host. Such a pipeline holds the steps directly. It is one stage with the name of the pipeline. A pipeline whose hosts have different roles, or that must finish on some hosts before it starts on others, has stages.
Order

Stages run in order. A stage starts when the previous stage finished on all its hosts. Inside a stage, each host runs its steps in order, without waiting for other hosts. A stage that matches no host is skipped. --stages runs only some stages, and --hosts only some hosts.
Steps of a stage
A step in a stage can use a module directly. It cannot use template, source, or the key of repo: those read the files of a recipe.
Failures
A failed host takes no part in later stages. The other hosts go on. A new run is the resume: steps that already succeeded check as ok.

# pipelines/site.yaml
stages:
  - name: base
    hosts: all
    parallelism: 1
    steps:
      - timezone:
          name: Etc/UTC
  - name: web
    hosts: web
    health:
      command: systemctl is-active nginx
      stable: 10
      timeout: 120
    steps:
      - recipe: nginx

# winch.yaml
name: acme
inventories:
  production:
    hosts:
      web1.acme.com: {}
      web2.acme.com: {}
    groups:
      web:
        hosts: [web1.acme.com, web2.acme.com]
recipes:
  nginx:
    steps:
      - pkg:
          name: nginx

keys.name: stages
keys.text: Stages in run order. A stage starts when the previous stage finished on all its hosts. A pipeline with stages has no other key.

keys.name: name
keys.text: Unique in the pipeline. It follows the rule of host names. --stages selects stages by name.

keys.name: hosts
keys.text: Host pattern. Run winch doc inventory for the patterns.

keys.name: parallelism
keys.line: maximum hosts at the same time
keys.text: Maximum hosts at the same time. Hosts start in inventory order. The next host starts when a host finishes the stage and its health gate passes. A failure stops new hosts from starting. Running hosts finish the stage.

keys.name: health
keys.line: check after a host changed in the stage
keys.text: Check after a host changed in the stage. The gate runs on a host after it finishes the stage, when the stage has a change on that host. The plan marks it with * and does not run it. A gate that fails stays pending on the host, and the next apply runs it.

keys.name: command
keys.text: Must exit 0. winch runs it on the host once per second until it exits 0, then keeps running it for stable seconds. A failed run starts the wait again. An exit of 126 or 127, when sh cannot find or run the command, fails the gate at once.

keys.name: stable
keys.text: Seconds the command keeps passing. It is less than timeout.

keys.name: timeout
keys.line: seconds the gate has to pass
keys.text: Seconds the gate has to pass. Then the host fails, and the error shows the end of the last output.

blocks.text: A recipe is a named group of steps that you can use again, with its own variables, templates, and files.
Files

A recipe is a directory in recipes/ with a recipe.yaml, and optional templates/ and files/ directories. Or it is a key in recipes of winch.yaml, without templates or files. winch loads every recipe for every command, also a recipe that no pipeline uses.
Names
A recipe name has lowercase letters, digits, and _. It can be the name of a module.
Running a recipe

A step runs a recipe with recipe: <name>. A recipe step has only name, recipe, vars, and when. A recipe runs at most once per host in a run. Two stages can run the same recipe when their hosts do not overlap. A recipe cannot run another recipe.
Templates and files
template reads from the templates/ directory of the recipe, and source from files/. Paths can name subdirectories. A template file uses the language of !tpl. Run winch doc templates.

# recipes/nginx/recipe.yaml
require:
  - !expr facts.os.id in ["debian", "ubuntu"]
vars:
  nginx_port: 80
steps:
  - pkg:
      name: nginx
  - name: Configure the site
    file:
      path: /etc/nginx/sites-enabled/default
      template: site.tmpl
      validate: nginx -t
    notify: reload
  - service:
      name: nginx
      running: true
      enabled: true
handlers:
  reload:
    - service:
        name: nginx
        reloaded: true

# recipes/nginx/templates/site.tmpl
server {
    listen {{ .vars.nginx_port }};
}

# winch.yaml
name: acme
hosts:
  web1.acme.com: {}
steps:
  - recipe: nginx
    vars:
      nginx_port: 8080

keys.name: require
keys.text: Conditions on facts, each an !expr. Every host where the recipe runs in the pipeline meets all of them, or it fails at plan. They see only facts.

keys.name: vars
keys.line: defaults of the recipe's own variables
keys.text: Defaults of the recipe's own variables. Their names start with the recipe name and _.

keys.name: steps
keys.text: Module steps, in order. A recipe cannot run another recipe.

keys.name: handlers
keys.line: steps that run after a change
keys.text: Steps that run after a change. They run after the last step of the recipe, when a step notified them. Run winch doc handlers.

blocks.text: A step is one action on a host: a module with its arguments, or a recipe.
Form

A step is a map. It has one module key, such as pkg or file, with the arguments of the module as a map. Or it has recipe with the name of a recipe. Run winch doc <module> for the arguments of a module.
Computed values
Any module argument can be a template or an expression, and so can then. when takes an expression. loop takes a list or an expression.
Evaluation

On each host, winch evaluates when. When it is false, winch skips the step. Then winch evaluates loop, and the arguments for each element. winch checks the step on the host, and apply changes what differs.
Results
A step that runs a command counts as changed: a cmd, and a service with restarted or reloaded. When a step fails, its host stops. Other hosts go on.
Key order
winch fmt puts the step keys in this order: name, the module or recipe, vars, when, loop, then, confirm_access, notify.

# winch.yaml
name: demo
hosts:
  web1.example.com: {}
vars:
  sites: [blog, shop]
steps:
  - name: Install nginx
    pkg:
      name: nginx
  - name: Write the sites
    file:
      path: !tpl /etc/nginx/sites-enabled/{{ .item }}.conf
      content: !tpl "# {{ .item }}\n"
    when: !expr len(vars.sites) > 0
    loop: !expr vars.sites
    then: nginx -t
    notify: reload
handlers:
  reload:
    - service:
        name: nginx
        reloaded: true

keys.name: name
keys.line: label in the plan and the logs
keys.text: Label in the plan and the logs. Without it, the plan shows the module and its main argument.

keys.name: recipe
keys.line: recipe to run, in place of a module
keys.text: Recipe to run, in place of a module. A recipe step has only name, recipe, vars, and when. A recipe runs at most once per host in a run.

keys.name: vars
keys.line: variable values for this recipe step
keys.text: Variable values for this recipe step. A value can be an !expr or a !tpl, and an !expr can use match(). They beat the inventory, and --set beats them. Only a recipe step has vars.

keys.name: when
keys.text: Skips the step when false. It is an !expr that gives true or false. winch evaluates none of the other keys of a skipped step. when runs once, before loop, and cannot use item.

keys.name: loop
keys.line: elements to run the step for, as item
keys.text: Elements to run the step for, as item. An !expr gives the list. loop: [] runs nothing and notifies nothing. A null element fails the host.

keys.name: then
keys.text: Command after a change. It runs right after the step changes something, before the next step. A failure of then fails the step. With loop, then runs once after the last element and cannot use item. A then that did not run stays pending on the host, and the next run runs it.

keys.name: confirm_access
keys.line: access check with rollback, for a service step
keys.text:
Access check with rollback, for a service step. Only a service step can use it, in steps or in handlers. A firewall step gets the same check without it.

Before the step, winch keeps the old state of each path that the changed steps of the recipe wrote or removed in this run. It starts a 60-second rollback timer in a process of its own.

After the step, winch runs the access check: it opens a new SSH connection and runs a command, through sudo -n when the login user is not root. It tries twice, 5 seconds apart.

When both tries fail, winch puts back the old files and runs daemon-reload after a unit file. It reverses a start or a stop of the step, and reloads or restarts the unit again. The host fails with the error "the access check failed: <error>; the old files are back". When the SSH connection ends first, winch rolls back as it ends. When the helper is gone, the timer rolls back.

When a run ends before a notified handler with confirm_access ran, winch puts back the files of that handler at once. The next run applies the change again.

A rollback puts back files only. It does not undo a change of a user or a group.

keys.name: notify
keys.line: handlers to run after a change
keys.text: Handlers to run after a change. Not a template or an expression. With loop, notify fires once when any element changed. Run winch doc handlers.

topics.name: handlers
topics.line: steps that run after a change

blocks.text: A handler is a list of steps that runs once, after a step that notifies it changes something.
Declaring a handler
handlers is a map in a recipe or in a stage. Each key is a handler name, and its value is a list of steps. A handler name has lowercase letters, digits, and _.
Notifying a handler

notify on a step names a handler of the current recipe or stage, or <recipe>.<handler> of another recipe. That recipe must run in the same pipeline, on at least one host where the step runs. On a host where it does not run, winch drops the notification.

# winch.yaml
name: demo
hosts:
  web1.example.com: {}
steps:
  - recipe: nginx
  - file:
      path: /etc/nginx/conf.d/gzip.conf
      content: "gzip on;\n"
    notify: nginx.reload
recipes:
  nginx:
    steps:
      - pkg:
          name: nginx
    handlers:
      reload:
        - service:
            name: nginx
            reloaded: true

# A change of gzip.conf reloads nginx once, at the end of the stage.
When a handler runs

items: A handler runs at most once per recipe run on a host. A handler of a stage runs at most once per stage run.
A handler runs after the last step of its recipe. When its recipe already ran on that host, it runs at the end of the current stage.
A handler of a stage runs after the last step of the stage and after the recipe handlers at the end of the stage. It runs before the health gate.
Handlers run in the order that the recipe or the stage declares them.

blocks.text: Handler steps
A handler step can have when. It cannot use notify or run a recipe. Only a handler step and winch run can use restarted and reloaded of service.
Pending handlers

When a step notifies a handler, winch marks the handler as pending on the host before the step changes anything. The mark goes when the handler succeeds. When a run stops first, or --stages leaves out the stage of its recipe, the handler stays pending. It runs the next time its recipe or stage runs on that host. The plan shows a handler that will run with "!". For a handler that the run does not reach, the plan shows a note, such as "a pending handler ssh.reload waits until its recipe runs on this host". The note is not a change.

topics.name: variables
topics.line: named values for hosts, groups, and recipes

blocks.text: Variables are named values that steps, templates, and expressions read.
Sources
Each host has its own value. A value comes from these sources. A later source replaces an earlier one:

items: the default
the vars of the groups of the host, then of the host
the vars of the recipe step
--set vars.<name>=<value>

blocks.text: Maps and lists do not merge.
Defaults

A default is declared once: in vars of winch.yaml, or in vars of the recipe that owns it. A recipe's own defaults start with the recipe name and _. A default can be a !secret, a template, or an expression. It sees vars, host, and facts, but not match(). A cycle between defaults is an error.
Variables without a default
A variable without a default needs no declaration. A read of it is enough, and the variable is required where it is read. A variable that may stay unset needs a default, such as relay_host: "".
Names and reads

A variable name has lowercase letters, digits, and _. A read names the variable: vars.domain, .vars.domain, $.vars.domain, or host.vars.domain. Any other read of the whole map, such as keys(vars) or range .vars, is an error. A map variable holds data that a step reads by key: vars.users[item]. host.vars holds the variables of the host without the vars of a recipe step.
Types

Variables have no types. A value keeps the type that YAML gives it. YAML reads 8.0 as 8 and 3.10 as 3.1. Quote such a value: php_version: "8.0". In the inventory, a default, or the vars of a recipe step, an unquoted one is a warning. --set parses its value as YAML, and there it is an error: --set 'vars.php_version="8.0"'.

# winch.yaml
name: demo
hosts:
  mail.acme.com:
    vars:
      relay_host: smtp.acme.com
  web1.acme.com: {}
groups:
  all:
    vars:
      admin_email: ops@acme.com
vars:
  domain: acme.com
  relay_host: ""
steps:
  - recipe: motd
    vars:
      motd_text: Managed by winch
recipes:
  motd:
    vars:
      motd_text: Welcome
    steps:
      - file:
          path: /etc/motd
          content: !tpl "{{ .vars.motd_text }} on {{ .vars.domain }}\n"
      - file:
          path: /etc/admin_email
          content: !tpl "{{ .vars.admin_email }}\n"
      - file:
          path: /etc/relay_host
          content: !tpl "{{ .vars.relay_host }}\n"
        when: !expr vars.relay_host != ""
A template is text in which winch fills in the values of each host.
Syntax
The !tpl tag marks a template, a Go text/template. It builds text, such as a path or a line. The template files of a recipe use the same language.
Data
A template reads these names with a leading dot:

rows: the variables of the host, with the vars of the recipe step
the facts of the host; run winch doc facts
name, short, address, groups, and vars of the host; address is the name when the host has no address
the current element in a step with loop

blocks.text: Inside range, "." is the element. $.vars reads the variables.
Where templates go
Any module argument can be a template or an expression, and so can then.
Functions and actions

A function takes its arguments after its name, separated by spaces: {{ join .vars.names ", " }}. Templates also have the actions of Go's text/template: if, else, range, with, define, template, block, break, and continue, and the variables $x := value.
Missing values

A template that reads a missing map key fails. Use get for a map key that may be missing. A variable needs a value or a default; get does not read the host's own .vars. A template that prints a null value fails.
Quoting

A value goes into a command as it is. Quote a value that must stay one word with quote. Quote a YAML value that starts with a quote, [, {, &, *, or !, or that contains ": " or " #". A template that starts with {{ needs quotes.
Other hosts
Templates have no match(). To list other hosts, give a recipe step a variable with an !expr that uses match(), and range over it in a template of the recipe.
When they run

winch evaluates templates on the machine that runs winch, during the plan. They cannot read the result of a step. winch checks each one when it loads the project: an unknown name or a syntax error is an error. An error while winch evaluates one for a host fails that host. The other hosts go on.

# winch.yaml
name: demo
hosts:
  web1.acme.com: {}
  web2.acme.com: {}
vars:
  sites: [blog, shop]
  admins: [ann, bob]
steps:
  - name: Write the sites
    file:
      path: !tpl /etc/nginx/sites-enabled/{{ .item }}.conf
      content: !tpl "server_name {{ .item }}.{{ .host.short }};\n"
    loop: !expr vars.sites
  - name: List the admins
    file:
      path: /etc/app/admins.conf
      content: !tpl "admins ={{ range .vars.admins }} {{ . }}{{ end }}\n"
  - name: List the other hosts
    recipe: peers
    vars:
      peers_hosts: !expr filter(match("all"), .name != host.name)
recipes:
  peers:
    steps:
      - file:
          path: /etc/peers
          content: !tpl "{{ range .vars.peers_hosts }}{{ .name }} {{ .address }}\n{{ end }}"

functions.name: and
functions.line: and x y: the first empty argument, or the last argument.
functions.text: and x y: the first empty argument, or the last argument. In an expression, and is an operator.

functions.name: call
functions.line: call f args: the result of the function f.
functions.text: call f args: the result of the function f. Project data holds no functions.

functions.name: eq
functions.line: eq a b: true when a equals b.
functions.text: eq a b: true when a equals b. With more arguments, true when a equals any of them. In an expression, use ==.

functions.name: ge
functions.line: ge a b: true when a >= b.
functions.text: ge a b: true when a >= b.

functions.name: get
functions.line: get m key: the value of key in the map m, or nothing when m has no such key.
functions.text: get m key: the value of key in the map m, or nothing when m has no such key. It reads a key that a map may leave out: {{ with get . "endpoint" }}Endpoint = {{ . }}{{ end }}. It does not read the host's own .vars: a variable that may have no value needs a default.

functions.name: gt
functions.line: gt a b: true when a > b.
functions.text: gt a b: true when a > b.

functions.name: has
functions.line: has list v: true when list contains v.
functions.text: has list v: true when list contains v. In an expression, use v in list.

blocks.text: An expression computes a value for each host, such as a list, a number, or true or false.
Syntax
The !expr tag marks an expression in the language of expr (expr-lang.org). Its result keeps its type: a list, a number, a boolean, a map, or a string.
Data
An expression reads these names without a leading dot:

rows: the variables of the host, with the vars of the recipe step
the facts of the host; run winch doc facts
name, short, address, groups, and vars of the host; address is the name when the host has no address
the current element in a step with loop
the hosts that match the host pattern p, with the fields of host

blocks.text: match(p) reads the inventory, not the --hosts selection. A host from match() has only the vars that need no facts. A default cannot use match().
Where expressions go
Any module argument can be an expression or a template, and so can then. when takes an expression. loop takes a list or an expression.
Operators

rows: membership in a list or a map
a, or b when a is nil
read an element or a key

blocks.text: Predicates
In a predicate, such as the second argument of filter, # is the element, and .name reads the key name of a map element: filter(vars.users, .uid >= 1000).
Missing values
A missing map key is nil. A module argument whose expression gives null fails the host.
Quoting
Quote a YAML value that starts with a quote, [, {, &, *, or !, or that contains ": " or " #".
When they run

winch evaluates expressions on the machine that runs winch, during the plan. They cannot read the result of a step. winch checks each one when it loads the project: an unknown name or a syntax error is an error. An error while winch evaluates one for a host fails that host. The other hosts go on. $env and now() are errors in every expression.

# winch.yaml
name: demo
hosts:
  mail.acme.com: {}
  web1.acme.com: {}
vars:
  mail_server: false
  domain: acme.com
  admins: [ann, bob]
  mailname: !expr 'vars.mail_server ? vars.domain : host.name'
steps:
  - name: Set the mail name
    file:
      path: /etc/mailname
      content: !expr 'vars.mailname + "\n"'
    when: !expr vars.mail_server
  - name: Add the admins
    user:
      name: !expr item
      groups: [sudo]
    loop: !expr sort(vars.admins)
  - name: List the other hosts
    file:
      path: /etc/peers
      content: !expr 'join(map(filter(match("all"), .name != host.name), .address), "\n") + "\n"'

topics.name: facts
topics.line: values that winch reads from each host

blocks.text: Facts are values that winch reads from each host before the plan, such as the OS release.
Reading a fact
Expressions read a fact as facts.os.id, and templates as {{ .facts.os.id }}. Facts are a fixed set. A read of an unknown fact is an error.

# winch.yaml
name: demo
hosts:
  web1.example.com: {}
steps:
  - recipe: base
recipes:
  base:
    require:
      - !expr facts.os.id == "debian" and facts.os.version == "13"
    steps:
      - reboot:
          if_required: true
        when: !expr facts.reboot_required

# The plan fails a host that is not Debian 13. A host that needs a
# reboot reboots.
When winch reads them
winch reads the facts once per host per run, before the first step, and again after a reboot. They describe the host before the run.

keys.name: os
keys.text: OS release of the host. winch reads id, version, and codename from /etc/os-release, or from /usr/lib/os-release when the first does not exist.

keys.name: id
keys.line: distribution, such as debian or ubuntu
keys.text: Distribution, such as debian or ubuntu.

keys.name: version
keys.text: Release number, such as 13 or 24.04. It is a string: compare it with a string, such as "13".

keys.name: codename
keys.line: release code name, such as trixie or noble
keys.text: Release code name, such as trixie or noble.

keys.name: arch
keys.text: CPU architecture: amd64 or arm64.

keys.name: reboot_required
keys.text: Pending reboot. It is true when /run/reboot-required exists, or when a kernel in /boot is newer than the running kernel.

blocks.text: A secret is a value that the project keeps encrypted. Only winch secret decrypt prints it.
Format
A secret is encrypted with age for the recipients in winch.yaml. The !secret tag marks it, followed by the ciphertext in base64 on one line.
Where a secret stands
A !secret stands only in a variable value: in the vars of an inventory, and in the defaults of winch.yaml and of recipes, at any depth of a list or a map. --set cannot give a secret.
Commands

rows: make an age key, add it to recipients
make a random password as a secret: write it at the path, or print it
encrypt a value from stdin or a prompt: write it at the path, or print it
print the plaintext of the secret at the path, or of a secret on stdin
encrypt all secrets for the current recipients

blocks.text: winch secret generate and winch secret encrypt need the recipients, but no age key. generate never prints the password.
winch secret encrypt reads a pipe on stdin. At a terminal, it asks for one line twice and does not show what you type. When the two values differ, it writes nothing.

winch secret decrypt needs the age key. It prints the plaintext and nothing else. It reads a !secret value on stdin, with or without the tag. A path to a map or to a value that is not a !secret is an error.
Paths
A path names a place in the project, with keys joined by ".". It works the same for an inventory or a recipe in its own file and as a key in winch.yaml.

rows: the default of x in winch.yaml
the default of mail_x in the recipe mail
the inventory at the top of winch.yaml
the key alice in the map variable users
the key acme.com in the map variable dkim_keys

items: The path ends at a variable value or below it in a map. A path cannot name a list item.
A key below the variable name that holds a dot or "[" stands in brackets and double quotes.
generate and encrypt replace the value at the path, and the output says replaced vars.x in winch.yaml. They add a missing path with the maps it needs, and the output says added vars.x in winch.yaml.
The inventory, the recipe, the host, and the group must exist. The group all always exists.
For generate and encrypt, something in the project must read the variable. A path that gives a variable a second default is an error.
The commands do not load the whole project, so errors in other places do not stop them.
generate and encrypt keep the comments and layout of the file. A flow map on the path, such as {a: 1}, is an error. They write through a symbolic link to the target.

blocks.text: The age key

winch secret init makes a key at ~/.config/winch/age.key, or at the path in WINCH_AGE_KEY. It makes a key only when no key is there. With WINCH_AGE_IDENTITY_CMD, it makes no key and adds the public key of the command's key.

winch reads the age key from the output of the command in WINCH_AGE_IDENTITY_CMD, such as op read op://infra/winch/key. Without it, winch reads the file in WINCH_AGE_KEY, or else ~/.config/winch/age.key. winch validate needs no age key.
A new member
A new member runs winch secret init and sends the change for review. The new key can read the secrets after a member who can read them runs winch secret rekey.
Output

A variable is secret when its value is a !secret, or when its default reads a secret variable. The plan, diffs, errors, logs, and JSON show (secret) in place of a secret, also a part of a value that comes from a secret. A filter replaces each secret value in all text that winch prints, also in output from the host. The filter also hides private keys, age keys, passwords in URLs, and well-known tokens.
Secrets in commands
A secret in a command does not show in the process list of the host. A program that the command starts with the secret as an argument, such as psql -c, does show it.
Warnings and errors

items: winch warns about text in project files that looks like a private key or a token, and is not a !secret.
winch warns about a file step whose content reads a secret and whose mode is missing or lets others read it. Inside a range, only the fields of the element that the body reads count, such as .name.
A !secret in a certbot hook is an error: certbot stores its hooks in a file that other users can read. A hook that reads a secret through match() fails the host.

blocks.text: A run of winch plans the changes, asks the question "Apply these changes?", and then applies them.
Plan and apply

winch plan shows the changes and changes nothing. winch apply shows the same plan, asks, and then makes the changes. For each host, the plan connects to the host, reads the facts, evaluates the steps, checks the requirements of the recipes, and checks each step on the host. Apply checks each step again right before it changes it. The second check decides.
Apply output

Apply prints a line for each step that changes or fails, then the summary. A step that checks as ok prints nothing: a planned change that the second check finds made, an assert that passes, and a handler restart that checks as ok. The summary line of plan and of apply counts hosts, not steps.
Plan marks

rows: unknown: a cmd step without creates or unless
a handler, or a pending then, gate, or assert that will run
a reboot, assert, or health gate that runs during apply

blocks.text: Plan hash

The last line of a plan is its hash, such as plan a3f9c2e1d07b4c58. The hash covers the project name, the hosts with the host name and port that ssh resolves for them and their login users, the stages, the evaluated steps, the check results, and the pending handlers and then commands. winch apply --check <hash> applies only when the new plan has that hash, without the question.
Without a terminal
apply without --yes or --check prints the plan and exits 5. Its last line is the command that applies that plan.
What winch changes

winch changes only what steps declare. Deleting a step changes nothing on the host. To remove a thing, declare it with absent: true. The plan fails a host when two steps manage the same path, package, unit, user, or group with different arguments.
Stopping and resuming

The first Ctrl-C lets the running step of each host finish, starts no new step, and ends with the summary. A second Ctrl-C ends the sessions with the hosts. A new run is the resume: steps that already succeeded check as ok, and pending handlers run.
Access to the host
winch keeps its access to each host.

items: A step that stops, disables, masks, or removes the SSH server fails: "this cuts off winch's access". So does a pkg or upgrade step that removes sudo while the login user is not root, or the package of the login user's shell.

Some steps get the rollback of confirm_access without it: a change of the login user's home directory, ~/.ssh, or any file in ~/.ssh, such as authorized_keys or rc, groups added to the login user, a change of /etc/pam.d, and a change of /etc/sudoers or /etc/sudoers.d when the login user is not root. Every firewall step gets it too. The plan marks such a step. Run winch doc step.confirm_access.

A step that changes sshd's config while ssh.socket is active, as on Ubuntu, restarts ssh.socket. It gets the same protection. sshd's config includes the unit files and drop-ins of ssh.service and ssh.socket in /etc/systemd/system.

Otherwise, a change of sshd's config gets no protection of its own. The plan warns at a step that loads the changed config without an access check, such as a restart of sshd without confirm_access, a reboot, or an upgrade of openssh-server. A then command such as systemctl restart ssh counts too, also on a step with confirm_access. The plan also warns when no later reload of sshd with confirm_access can roll the change back. Reload sshd in a service handler with confirm_access: true.
After the last step of a host that changed something, winch checks the access once more. When it fails, the host fails, and nothing rolls back.

blocks.text: Changing the SSH port
The access check connects to the port in your SSH config. So a change of sshd's Port in one run always rolls back. Move sshd to a new port in three runs:

items: Let sshd listen on the old and the new port.
Change the port in the SSH config.
Remove the old port from sshd.

blocks.text: Exit codes

rows: invalid command line or project; nothing ran
one or more hosts were unreachable, and no step failed
winch cannot ask the question; nothing changed
the plan hash differs from --check; nothing changed

blocks.text: When several apply, the first in the order 3, 1, 4, 6, 5, 2, 0 wins.
JSON output
--json writes one JSON object per line on stdout. Each has type and time. The types:

rows: an error, a warning, or a note, with severity, file, line, col, and message; a note about a host has host
a host finished, failed, or was unreachable
the output of winch exec on one host
the counts, the plan hash, and the exit code; always last

blocks.text: A step event has host and address, such as mail.acme.com:nginx#3[0]: the host, the stage or recipe, the step number from 1, and the loop index from 0.

winch plan site
winch apply site
winch apply site --check a3f9c2e1d07b4c58
winch plan site --exit-code

topics.name: remote
topics.line: how winch reaches a host and runs there

blocks.text: winch works on a host through one SSH connection, the session, with a helper program at the other end.
What a host needs

items: Debian 13, Ubuntu 24.04, or Ubuntu 26.04, on amd64 or arm64.
Login as root, or as a user with passwordless sudo.
A POSIX login shell that prints nothing on stdout before winch starts a command.
/var/lib/winch/ on a file system that allows running programs.

blocks.text: Nothing else needs to be installed. The machine that runs winch is Linux or macOS with the OpenSSH client.
SSH settings

winch runs your ssh, so ~/.ssh/config applies: Port, IdentityFile, ProxyJump, and every other setting. Its Host blocks match the host name of the inventory, also when the host has an address. The address and the user of the inventory override the SSH config. --user overrides both.

# ~/.ssh/config
Host *.acme.com
  Port 2222
  IdentityFile ~/.ssh/acme_ed25519

# inventories/production.yaml
hosts:
  web1.acme.com:
    address: 192.0.2.10
    user: admin

# winch logs in to 192.0.2.10 on port 2222 as admin,
# with the key ~/.ssh/acme_ed25519.

ssh_config in winch.yaml names another SSH config file, relative to the project directory. winch passes it with -F to every ssh it runs: the sessions, the access checks, and each hop of a ProxyJump. ssh then reads this file instead of ~/.ssh/config. Use it for the SSH config that a tool such as Lima or Vagrant writes. To keep ~/.ssh/config, include it:

# winch.yaml
name: acme
ssh_config: ssh_config

# ssh_config
Include ~/.ssh/config
Include ~/.lima/default/ssh.config
winch also passes these options. They win over the SSH config:

rows: a host that does not answer fails and does not hang the run
a master connection from the SSH config, with its own keepalive, is not used
the SSH config does not replace or add to the command of winch

blocks.text: Host keys and passphrases

When stdin and stderr are terminals, ssh can ask for a new host key or a key passphrase. Sessions then start one at a time, in inventory order, so each question belongs to one host. After the start, hosts run in parallel.

Without a terminal, or with --batch, winch passes BatchMode=yes and sessions start in parallel. A host that needs a question is then unreachable. Accept the host key and load the key into ssh-agent first:

ssh -o HostName=192.0.2.10 -l admin web1.acme.com
ssh-add ~/.ssh/acme_ed25519
winch apply site --batch

# ssh asks no questions; the apply question stays.

The access checks and the connections after a reboot always use BatchMode=yes, so they cannot ask for anything. Run winch doc workflow for the access checks. At a terminal, a session therefore logs in with BatchMode=yes first. When the host refuses that login, or its host key is new, winch logs in again, and ssh can ask. A host that refused the first login plans as usual, but apply stops before its first change and names ssh-add. After a new host key, apply runs one access check before the first change.
When a connection fails

A host is unreachable when ssh fails before the session starts: the name does not resolve, the connection is refused or takes more than 15 seconds, or the host key or the login fails. winch then exits 4 when no step failed. For an unknown host key, the error names the ssh command to run once. For a refused login, it names ssh-add.
Only one winch run works on a host at a time. When another run holds the host, the error names that run and the process ID of its helper. When that run is gone, end the process.
The session

A session is one ssh process with the helper at the other end. All work on a host goes through it. It opens at the first work of the host and stays open across stages and through the question. The host lock stays held while the question waits; Ctrl-C releases it. A session closes when its host has no more work. The access checks open their own connections.
winch keeps the helper in /var/lib/winch/bin/ and sends it when it is missing. The helper exits when the session ends and leaves no process, except a confirm_access timer until it ends.
The helpers for amd64 and arm64 are inside the winch binary. A winch built with go install has none: plan, apply, run, and exec fail before they contact a host. Install a release.
How commands run
Every command on the host, also one that a module runs, such as apt-get or systemctl, runs as root in /, with only this environment:
Nothing comes from the login session, such as the TMPDIR that libpam-tmpdir sets.
The commands of cmd, assert, unless, validate, then, health, and the certbot hooks run through sh -e, with stdin from /dev/null. A command of several lines stops at its first failed line.

A cmd with dir runs in that directory. A cmd with user runs as that user, with the home of that user as HOME, and its name as USER and LOGNAME. It starts no login session: PAM does not run, so the login umask and limits of the user do not apply.
The time limit

A command stops after 10 minutes, after the timeout of a cmd step in seconds, or after the --timeout of winch exec. The helper sends SIGTERM to the command and its child processes, and SIGKILL 10 seconds later to those that still run. The step fails, and the error shows the last 10 lines of output. apt-get in pkg, repo, and upgrade has no time limit.

When the session ends, the helper lets the running command finish within its limit, and then exits. A package install is not cut off in the middle. winch exec is different: on Ctrl-C, or when its session breaks, its command gets SIGINT, and SIGKILL after 10 seconds.
What winch leaves on the host
winch keeps its files in /var/lib/winch/:

rows: the masked content of each file that holds a secret
the package index that the plan reads, the sources it plans with, and the archives that a session fetches
checksum, owner, and group of each unpack
the firewall table after its last load
old files for confirm_access, during a run
the boot ID and the error of a failed reboot, until the next boot

blocks.text: To remove winch from a host, delete /var/lib/winch/. Pending handlers, then commands, health gates, asserts, and certbot hooks are then lost. The next run of winch starts from the state of the host.

modules.name: assert
modules.line: stop a host when a check command fails
modules.body: The plan marks the step with * and runs nothing. Apply runs the command. A failed assert stays pending on the host, and the next apply runs it again, also when nothing else changes.

keys.name: command
keys.text: Check command. It runs during apply, through sh -e as root, in /. Exit 0 passes.

keys.name: message
keys.text: Error when the check fails. The host fails with it when the command exits non-zero, followed by the shell's error when the exit is 126 or 127.

modules.example:
- name: Check that nginx answers
  assert:
    command: curl -fsS http://localhost/
    message: nginx does not answer on port 80

modules.name: certbot
modules.body: The step runs certbot certonly. Renewal stays with certbot's own timer. Install the package certbot in an earlier pkg step. The nginx and apache authenticators also need python3-certbot-nginx or python3-certbot-apache.

keys.name: name
keys.text: Certificate name in /etc/letsencrypt.

keys.name: domains
keys.text: No wildcards. A wildcard needs a DNS challenge.

keys.name: email
keys.text: Let's Encrypt account address.

keys.name: authenticator
keys.text: Challenge plugin: nginx, apache, standalone, or webroot. The nginx and apache plugins do not change the config of the web server. When a challenge runs, they reload it, and the plan says so. standalone binds port 80 itself; pre_hook and post_hook can stop and start what holds that port. webroot needs webroot_path.

keys.name: webroot_path
keys.text: Web root for webroot.

keys.name: pre_hook
keys.text: Command before each try to get a certificate. certbot stores it in a file that other users can read, so it cannot hold a secret. A hook that needs a secret reads it from a root-only file that a file step writes.

keys.name: post_hook
keys.text: Command after each try to get a certificate. certbot stores it in a file that other users can read, so it cannot hold a secret.

keys.name: deploy_hook
keys.text: Command after each new certificate, also the first. A failed hook fails the step, and the next apply runs it again. It cannot hold a secret.

keys.name: reuse_key
keys.line: keep the private key at renewal
keys.text: Keep the private key at renewal.

modules.example:
- certbot:
    name: mail
    domains: [mail.example.com]
    email: admin@example.com
    deploy_hook: systemctl reload postfix

modules.name: cmd
modules.body: Without creates or unless, the check result is unknown, and apply runs the command each time. A secret in the command does not show in the process list of the host. A program that the command starts with the secret as an argument, such as psql -c, does show it.

keys.name: command
keys.text: Shell script. It runs through sh -e as root, in /, with stdin from /dev/null. A script of several lines stops at its first failed line. Without creates or unless, the check result is unknown.

keys.name: creates
keys.line: path that marks the work as done
keys.text: Path that marks the work as done. The step is ok when the path exists. When the command exits 0 and the path is still missing, the step fails. The path has no glob characters. A step has at most one of creates and unless.

keys.name: unless
keys.line: check command; exit 0 skips the step
keys.text: Check command; exit 0 skips the step. It runs at the check as root, in /, with the timeout of the step. user and dir do not apply to it. A step has at most one of creates and unless.

keys.name: user
keys.text: Account that runs command. Its home is HOME. The step starts no login session: PAM does not run, so the login umask and limits of the account do not apply, and the umask is 022.

keys.name: dir
keys.text: Working directory.

keys.name: timeout
keys.line: limit in seconds, also for unless
keys.text: Limit in seconds, also for unless. After it, winch stops the command and the step fails.

modules.example:
- name: Build the alias database
  cmd:
    command: newaliases
    creates: /etc/aliases.db

modules.name: debconf
modules.body:
Only the scripts of a package read its answers. Put the step before the pkg step that installs the package, also when the package comes in as a dependency.

After a package loaded the question, as at its install, the check compares type with the type of the question. A select or multiselect value must be one of the choices of the question. A type that differs, or a value that is not a choice, fails the check.

keys.name: package
keys.text: Package that asks the question.

keys.name: question
keys.text: Name, such as postfix/main_mailer_type.

keys.name: type
keys.line: question type, such as string, boolean, or select
keys.text: Question type, such as string, boolean, or select.

keys.name: value
keys.text: Answer, as text. Only the scripts of the package read it, so put the step before the pkg step that installs the package.

modules.example:
- debconf:
    package: postfix
    question: postfix/main_mailer_type
    type: select
    value: Internet Site

modules.name: dir
modules.body: The step creates missing parent directories, owned by root with mode 0755. winch checks owner, group, and mode on every run.

keys.name: path
keys.text: Absolute. The step creates missing parent directories, owned by root with mode 0755. It follows a symbolic link to a directory and manages the directory behind it.

keys.name: owner
keys.text: A user name, or a numeric ID that needs no account. A value of only digits is an ID, also in quotes.

keys.name: group
keys.text: A group name, or a numeric ID that needs no group. A value of only digits is an ID, also in quotes.

keys.name: mode
keys.text: Octal, in quotes: "0750". Without quotes, YAML reads it as a number.

keys.name: recurse
keys.line: owner and group for the whole tree
keys.text: Owner and group for the whole tree. The mode stays the mode of the directory alone. The plan fails when another step gives a path in the tree another owner or group; a file with content and no owner counts as root.

keys.name: absent
keys.text: Remove it with its content.

keys.name: replace
keys.line: remove another kind of thing at path first
keys.text: Remove another kind of thing at path first, such as a file or a link. Without it, such a thing fails the check.

keys.name: purge
keys.text: Remove entries that nothing declares. Purge looks only at the direct entries. It keeps an entry that a package owns, or that a step for the host writes. Each removal is a change.

keys.name: keep
keys.text: Name patterns that purge keeps, such as *.db. They are glob patterns. keep needs purge.

modules.example:
- dir:
    path: /var/www/app
    owner: www-data
    group: www-data
    mode: "0750"

modules.name: download
modules.line: download a file or an archive
modules.body: The host fetches the file and checks its sha256. A download with another checksum fails and keeps the old file. A step has path or unpack.

keys.name: url
keys.text: Fetched by the host.

keys.name: sha256
keys.text: Checksum of the file. Take the value from the checksum file that the vendor publishes, or download the file once and run sha256sum on it. A download with another checksum fails and keeps the old file.

keys.name: path
keys.line: absolute target of a single file
keys.text: Absolute target of a single file. A step has path or unpack.

keys.name: unpack
keys.text: Directory for the unpacked archive. The path of the URL ends in .tar.gz, .tgz, .tar.xz, or .zip. The directory holds the entries of the archive as they are: a top directory of the archive stays, as in <unpack>/app-1.2/bin. The step unpacks again when sha256, owner, group, or the directory changes. Each unpack replaces the whole tree, also the first: it removes the files that are already in the directory. Keep the files that a program writes, such as its config, data, and logs, outside the directory.

keys.name: owner
keys.line: of the file or the unpacked tree
keys.text: Of the file or the unpacked tree. A user name or a numeric ID.

keys.name: group
keys.line: of the file or the unpacked tree
keys.text: Of the file or the unpacked tree. A group name or a numeric ID.

keys.name: mode
keys.text: Octal, in quotes; path only. Without quotes, YAML reads it as a number. With unpack, mode is an error: the entries keep the modes of the archive, without write permission for group and others.

modules.example:
- download:
    url: https://example.com/releases/app-1.4.2-linux-amd64
    sha256: 9f86d081884c7d659a2feaa0c55ad015a3bf4f1b2b0b822cd15d6c15b0f00a08
    path: /usr/local/bin/app
    mode: "0755"

modules.name: file
modules.body: At most one of content, template, source, copy_from, and stock sets the content. A step without any of them manages only the owner, group, and mode that it gives, of a file that exists. The step creates missing parent directories, owned by root with mode 0755.

keys.name: path
keys.text: Absolute. The step creates missing parent directories, owned by root with mode 0755.

keys.name: content
keys.text: Literal text. A step without content, template, source, copy_from, or stock sets only the owner, group, and mode that it gives, with no defaults, of a file that exists. When that file is missing, the plan says does not exist yet. Apply fails when it is still missing.

keys.name: template
keys.text: File in the recipe's templates/ directory. Its output is the content.

keys.name: source
keys.text: File in the recipe's files/ directory. Its bytes are the content.

keys.name: copy_from
keys.text: File on the host. Its bytes are the content. Its permission bits, without the write bits of the group and others, are the default mode. The default owner and group stay root: the owner of the source does not carry over.

keys.name: stock
keys.text: Content that the package ships for path, from the installed version. The package also gives the default owner, group, and mode.

keys.name: owner
keys.text: A user name or a numeric ID. A step without content has no default.

keys.name: group
keys.text: A group name or a numeric ID. A step without content has no default.

keys.name: mode
keys.text: Octal, in quotes: "0640". Without quotes, YAML reads it as a number. With stock, the package gives the default. With copy_from, the source gives it, without the write bits of the group and others. A step without content has no default.

keys.name: validate
keys.line: check command for the new file
keys.text: Check command for the new file. The command names the real path, or checks the whole config: nginx -t. winch puts the new file in place and runs the command. When the command fails, the old file comes back and the step fails.

keys.name: absent
keys.text: Remove the file. A path of another kind fails the check.

keys.name: replace
keys.line: remove another kind of thing at path first
keys.text: Remove another kind of thing at path first, such as a directory. Without it, such a thing fails the check.

modules.example:
- name: Write the message of the day
  file:
    path: /etc/motd
    content: "Welcome to mail.example.com.\n"
    mode: "0644"

modules.name: firewall
modules.body:
The step owns the nftables table inet winch and changes no other table. The rules of Docker, fail2ban, or /etc/nftables.conf stay. Its input chain filters traffic to the host. Traffic that Docker forwards to a container passes the forward hook, so a port that Docker publishes stays open. Publish the port on 127.0.0.1 when only a local proxy reaches the container. A host has at most one firewall step in a run.

The step needs nft: install the package nftables in an earlier pkg step.

Every change gets the access check and the rollback of confirm_access. When the access check fails after the new rules load, the old rules come back.

The check fails when a file of the step on the host, such as /etc/winch/firewall.nft, is larger than 1 MiB.

keys.name: allow
keys.line: accepted traffic to the host; the host drops the rest
keys.text: Accepted traffic to the host; the host drops the rest. It always accepts established and related traffic, loopback, ICMP echo requests, the ICMPv6 types that IPv6 needs, and DHCP replies. It drops invalid packets.

keys.name: tcp
keys.text: Ports. A rule has tcp or udp.

keys.name: udp
keys.text: Ports. A rule has tcp or udp.

keys.name: from
keys.text: Source addresses or networks. IPv4 and IPv6 are allowed. Without from, the rule accepts every source.

keys.name: absent
keys.line: remove the table, its file, and its unit
keys.text: Remove the table, its file, and its unit.

modules.name: group

keys.name: name
keys.text: A new group's name has lowercase letters, digits, _, and -, and does not start with a digit or -. It has at most 32 characters.

keys.name: gid
keys.text: A whole number. A gid that another group has fails the check.

keys.name: system
keys.text: System group, at creation only. It counts only when the step creates the group.

keys.name: absent
keys.text: Remove the group. The check fails when the group is the primary group of a user.

modules.example:
- group:
    name: deploy
    system: true

modules.name: hostname
modules.body: The check compares name with the static name in /etc/hostname and with the running name. When one of them differs, the step sets the name.

keys.name: name
keys.text: Short name, such as mail.

modules.example:
- hostname:
    name: mail

modules.name: line
modules.line: manage one line in a file

keys.name: path
keys.text: Absolute. A missing file is a change in the plan, since an earlier step can create it. Apply fails when it is still missing.

keys.name: line
keys.text: Line to keep. It replaces the one line that match finds, or goes at the end of the file.

keys.name: match
keys.text: Regular expression for the line. More than one matching line fails the check.

keys.name: validate
keys.text: Check command, as for file. It runs with absent too.

keys.name: absent
keys.text: Remove the matching lines.

modules.example:
- line:
    path: /etc/default/grub
    match: ^GRUB_TIMEOUT=
    line: GRUB_TIMEOUT=2
  then: update-grub

modules.name: link
modules.body: The step creates missing parent directories, owned by root with mode 0755.

keys.name: path
keys.text: Absolute. The step creates missing parent directories, owned by root with mode 0755.

keys.name: target
keys.line: relative or absolute; need not exist
keys.text: Relative or absolute; need not exist.

keys.name: validate
keys.text: Check command, as for file.

keys.name: absent
keys.text: Remove the link. A path of another kind fails the check.

keys.name: replace
keys.line: remove another kind of thing at path first
keys.text: Remove another kind of thing at path first, such as a file or a directory. Without it, such a thing fails the check.

modules.example:
- link:
    path: /etc/nginx/sites-enabled/app
    target: /etc/nginx/sites-available/app

modules.name: pkg
modules.body: Before the first install of a run on a host, apply refreshes the package index. After a repo step changed something, the next pkg step refreshes it again.

keys.name: name
keys.text: Installed in one apt call.

keys.name: recommends
keys.text: Install recommended packages too.

keys.name: purge
keys.text: Remove the config files too. purge needs absent.

keys.name: absent
keys.text: Remove the packages.

modules.example:
- pkg:
    name: [nginx, certbot]
    recommends: false

modules.name: reboot

keys.name: if_required
keys.text: Only on a pending reboot. With false, the step always reboots.

keys.name: timeout
keys.text: Wait limit in seconds.

modules.example:
- reboot:
    if_required: true

modules.name: repo
modules.body: The check fails when the source file or the key file on the host is larger than 1 MiB.

keys.name: name
keys.text: File name in /etc/apt, of the source file and of the key file.

keys.name: url
keys.line: without a user or a password
keys.text: Without a user or a password.

keys.name: suite
keys.text: Such as trixie. A flat suite ends in /.

keys.name: components
keys.text: Such as main. They are required, except for a flat suite, which has none.

keys.name: key
keys.line: key file in the recipe's files/
keys.text: Key file in the recipe's files/ directory: an ASCII-armored OpenPGP public key. Download the vendor's key once and keep it in the project. A step has at most one of key and key_content.

keys.name: key_content
keys.line: key text, in place of key
keys.text: Key text, in place of key: an ASCII-armored OpenPGP public key. A step has at most one of key and key_content.

modules.example:
- repo:
    name: nginx
    url: https://nginx.org/packages/debian
    suite: trixie
    components: [nginx]
    key: key.asc

modules.name: service
modules.body:
With running: false, a missing unit file is ok, with the note <unit> does not exist. A service step with confirm_access: true runs the access check after the step, and rolls back when it fails. Run winch doc step.confirm_access. In a handler, restarted and reloaded check as ok when a service step of the run started the unit after the handler's last notify, no earlier step of the handler changed anything, and the step has no confirm_access.

A unit of type simple, exec, forking, or idle does not report readiness. After its start or restart, apply watches it for 2 seconds. A reload of such a unit without ExecReload is a restart, and gets the watch. The step fails when the unit is not running then, or when systemd restarted it in that time. A unit that crashes after the 2 seconds passes. A reload ends when ExecReload ends: one that only sends a signal is confirmed as sent, and the unit can still end after it. A health gate checks that a service works. Run winch doc pipeline.health.

keys.name: name
keys.text: Unit, with or without .service, such as nginx or certbot.timer.

keys.name: running
keys.line: start or stop; unset leaves it
keys.text: Start or stop; unset leaves it. Without running, the step does not start or stop the unit.

keys.name: enabled
keys.line: start at boot; unset leaves it
keys.text: Start at boot; unset leaves it. Without enabled, the step does not change it.

keys.name: reloaded

modules.name: unit
modules.body:
A change of the file, also of its owner or mode, runs systemctl daemon-reload. daemon-reload does not restart a running unit. A handler with restarted: true does.

The step also checks an ok file: systemd can still need a reload, as after a run that wrote the file and then failed. Then the step runs daemon-reload as a change, so its handlers run. A template unit, such as app@.service, skips this check.

keys.name: name
keys.text: File name with its type, such as app.service or app@.service.

keys.name: source
keys.text: File in the recipe's files/ directory. A step has source or content.

keys.name: content
keys.text: Unit file text. A step has source or content.

modules.example:
- unit:
    name: app.service
    content: |
      [Unit]
      Description=App

      [Service]
      ExecStart=/usr/local/bin/app

      [Install]
      WantedBy=multi-user.target

modules.name: upgrade
modules.body: The step refreshes the package index, also during the plan, and checks for pending upgrades.

keys.name: mode
keys.text: Safe or full. safe installs the upgrades that remove no package. full also installs the upgrades that add or remove packages.

modules.example:
- upgrade:
    mode: safe

modules.name: user
modules.body: A step that creates a user also creates its home directory. Without group, it also creates a group with the name of the user. The defaults and system count only when the step creates the user.

keys.name: name
keys.text: A new user's name has lowercase letters, digits, _, and -, and does not start with a digit or -. It has at most 32 characters.

keys.name: uid
keys.text: A whole number. A uid that another user has fails the check.

keys.name: group
keys.text: Primary group. Without group, a step that creates the user also creates a group with the name of the user.

keys.name: system
keys.text: System user, at creation only. Its home is /nonexistent and its shell is /usr/sbin/nologin. It counts only when the step creates the user.

keys.name: home
keys.text: Created when missing; never moved. The step creates a missing home directory, except /nonexistent. The default counts only when the step creates the user. A system user gets /nonexistent. A changed home is not moved.

keys.name: shell
keys.text: Login shell. The default counts only when the step creates the user. A system user gets /usr/sbin/nologin.

keys.name: groups
keys.text: Exact supplementary groups. A step has groups or add_groups.

keys.name: add_groups
keys.line: groups to join, keeping the others
keys.text: Groups to join, keeping the others. A step with only name and add_groups does not create the user: apply fails when the user does not exist.

keys.name: password
keys.text: Crypt hash, usually a !secret, such as one from mkpasswd -m yescrypt or openssl passwd -6. ! or * alone locks the password. Without password, the password of a new user is locked.

keys.name: comment
keys.text: Full name or description.

keys.name: authorized_keys
keys.line: exact SSH keys of the user
keys.text: Exact SSH keys of the user, in ~/.ssh/authorized_keys.

keys.name: absent
keys.line: remove the user; the home stays
keys.text: Remove the user; the home stays.

modules.example:
- user:
    name: deploy
    groups: [www-data]
    shell: /bin/bash
    authorized_keys:
      - ssh-ed25519 AAAAC3NzaC1lZDI1NTE5AAAAIGlrZDl2Q3h5c3d6bW9ja2tleWZvcmRvY3MxMjM0 deploy@laptop

commands.name: fmt
description: Fmt fixes the indentation and the step key order of the project files: winch.yaml, the inventories, the pipelines, and the recipes.
It indents with two spaces, and indents list items under their key.

It puts step keys in this order: name, the module or recipe key, vars, when, loop, then, confirm_access, notify. Steps in flow style keep their key order. A comment above a key that moves to the first place goes above the "-" of its step.
It keeps comments, blank lines, quoting, anchors, flow style, and line ends. It writes a file only when the result decodes to the same values. It prints each file that it changes.
When a file does not parse, or fmt cannot keep the layout of a file, fmt shows the error, exits with code 3, and changes no file.

commands.name: apply
commands.summary: make the changes after you approve the plan
description: Apply shows the plan of a pipeline, asks the question "Apply these changes?", and then makes the changes.
Leave out the pipeline name when the steps are at the top of winch.yaml.

winch asks only when stdin and stderr are terminals. Without a terminal, and without --yes or --check, apply prints the plan and exits with code 5. Its last line is the command that applies the plan with its hash.
--check replaces the question. When the new plan has another hash, apply exits with code 6 and changes nothing.

commands.name: run
commands.summary: plan and apply one module step
description: Run plans one module step on the hosts of the pattern, asks, and applies it.
A host pattern is a group or a host, with "," for union, "&" for intersection, and "!" for exclusion.

Each value parses as YAML: name=[htop,curl] is a list. Quote a value that YAML would change, such as mode='"0644"'. A value that YAML rejects, such as *x, @x, or [x, is an error that says to quote it.

commands.name: exec
commands.summary: run a shell command on hosts
description: Exec runs a shell command on the hosts of the pattern, in parallel, and shows its output. It makes no plan and asks no question.
A host pattern is a group or a host, with "," for union, "&" for intersection, and "!" for exclusion.
winch joins the words after -- with spaces and runs them through sh -c as root, in /, with stdin from /dev/null.
When the project has secrets, exec needs the age key. It decrypts the secrets, so that its output hides them.

Each host shows one block: the host name, then the output. Hosts with the same output and exit code share one block. A command that exits non-zero adds "exit status N" to its block. winch exits with code 1 when the command fails on a host.
With --json, each host gives one exec event with output and exit_code.
The command stops after 600 seconds, or after --timeout. Each host then sends SIGTERM to the command, and SIGKILL 10 seconds later.
Ctrl-C stops the commands. Each host sends SIGINT to the command, and SIGKILL when it still runs after 10 seconds.
With a terminal, ssh can ask questions, and winch connects to the hosts one at a time. Without one, or with --batch, ssh asks nothing, and winch connects to them in parallel.

description: Init makes an age key when there is none, prints its public key, and adds the public key to recipients in winch.yaml when it is not in the list.
The key is the file that WINCH_AGE_KEY names, or else ~/.config/winch/age.key. A new key gets mode 0600, and its directory 0700.

commands.name: secret generate
commands.summary: make a random password as a secret
description: Generate makes a random password of 32 letters and digits and encrypts it for the recipients in winch.yaml. With a path, it writes the !secret value at the path; without one, it prints it. It never prints the password.

A path names a place in the project, with keys joined by ".". vars.x is the default of x in winch.yaml, and recipes.mail.vars.mail_x a default in the recipe mail. groups.all.vars.x and hosts.web1.vars.x are in the inventory at the top of winch.yaml, and inventories.prod.groups.all.vars.x is in the inventory prod. A path can go on into a map variable, such as vars.users.alice, but not into a list. A key with dots or "[" stands in brackets and double quotes, such as vars.dkim_keys["acme.com"].

The command replaces the value at the path, or adds a missing path with the maps it needs. The inventory, the recipe, the host, and the group must exist; the group all always exists. Something in the project must read the variable, and a variable has one default. The file keeps its comments and layout.
